doc.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022

chapter: Denver youth and University of Denver
title: Picking up saxophone at 16 and first gigs
summary: He kept clarinet and sax separate, played his first gig on New Year's Eve five weeks after starting sax, and later drove far for $15 gigs.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah I was one of those guys, yeah. I started out on clarinet and I always sort of kept the two tracks separate, you know I played clarinet and did all the legit stuff, the classical stuff, and at age 16 I picked up the saxophone and I remember five weeks later I played my first gig, it was New Year’s Eve.
That was my first gig too.
Yeah. And the rest is history.
And you got to play “Auld Lang Syne” for the first time, I wonder if you used the Guy Lombardo vibrato?
I was playing second tenor someplace so I probably did, just follow the lead guy.
Did you feel, can you remember what you made that night?

You know I remember even a little after that, in college, we would get in our cars and we would drive to Goodland, Kansas or Scottsbluff, Nebraska, or Cheyenne, Wyoming or sometimes Laramie, Wyoming. You know we’d drive there for fifteen bucks, you know? It took us all — you know, we’d go there, we left in the afternoon, play the gig, come back at night, get home around, you know, five or six in the morning. It was crazy.
